text:
incident-bot: ALERT 13:02 UTC - spike in 5xx and sustained token rate on /v1/embeddings across prod-us-east-1. Error rate 4.8% p50 lat 210ms p95 2.3s p99 9.1s. Possible downstream throttling on storage nodes.

mike: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking which customers are spiking. tagging @sophia for infra visibility.

sophia: thanks. looking at infra metrics now — observed a surge of large embedding jobs (batch sizes 512-1024) from a handful of API keys, plus elevated KV cache miss rates.

samir: confirmed, routing queue is backing up for embeddings workers, cpu on model-serving pods at 95%. chat and rerank endpoints look fine.

mike: ok decision tree: 1) apply immediate per-endpoint mitigation to stop the downstream overload 2) narrow to offending API keys if feasible 3) notify CS.

anna: customer-impact note — Support: several customers reported timeouts on embedding jobs. marking high-priority for those with active SLAs.

mike: mitigation I can do right now: apply per-endpoint rate limit to embeddings route to protect runtime. lowering global embeddings RPS to 60 and lowering per-key concurrency. executing now.

mike: running internal CLI to change route limits:
```
# redwoodctl patch-route-limit 
redwoodctl patch-route-limit --route "/v1/embeddings" --limit-rps 60 --limit-concurrency 5 --note "emergency throttle due to high token rate"
```

deploy-bot: deploy accepted by control plane, policy push started.

sophia: policy applied to prod-us-east-1. routing saw immediate drop in inflight for embeddings workers. p99 latency now falling.

mike: also enabled soft-quota for large-batch requests to prefer queuing vs failing for well-behaved customers. command:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/quotas" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings","quota_type":"batch_size","max":256,"action":"queue"}'
```

samir: good call. I also blacklisted one API key that's clearly dump-queuing oversized batches without backoff. key id: key_9xYz. Blocked for 10m to reduce churn.

anna: Support: notifying top affected customers and offering retry guidance. drafting message: "We're applying temporary rate limits to embeddings to restore service; if you rely on large batch jobs, please reduce batch size or reach out to support for quota exceptions."

mike: monitoring — p95 error rate down to 0.9% within 6 minutes of throttle. token throughput reduced ~70%. chat and rerank unaffected.

sophia: followups: 1) schedule a tighter per-route SLA guard so embeddings can't starve other routes 2) add alert rule for sustained large-batch ingestion per API key 3) consider default cap on batch_size for embeddings endpoints.

mike: creating incident ticket and tagging engineering owners. Incident ticket: INC-2026-1934. please add timeline and commands used.

samir: I'll add a temporary routing policy that prefers smaller-quantized model variants for non-critical embeddings to lower cpu/memory footprint. will coordinate with model team.

anna: handoff note for next oncall shift (sophia takes over at 14:00 UTC): mitigation applied, blacklisted key_9xYz for 10m, global embeddings RPS=60, per-key concurrency=5, batch_size soft-queue <=256. customer outreach in progress.

mike: leaving detailed runbook steps in the ticket. if metrics remain stable for 30m, we'll lift blacklist and gradually raise embeddings RPS to 200 with auto-throttle profiles.

sophia: ack, will monitor for the next hour and escalate if error rate >1.5% or server CPU >85%.

deploy-bot: automated note — policy push completed at 13:08 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation in place, partial customer impact, oncall handoff scheduled.

mike: closing thread from my side, handing to sophia. :white_check_mark:

sophia: taking over. logging final snapshot and adding retrospective action items (route-specific quotas, per-key ingestion alarms, default batch caps).
